correctness.rationale: Independently reconstruct the identity by restricting a partition to its unmarked labels, giving rho. Choose j of the k marked labels to join blocks of rho; each has signed sum e(rho)-o(rho) over its possible target blocks because the block sign in terms of marked and unmarked sizes a,b is (-1)^(ab). The remaining marked labels contribute the ordinary Bell number B_(k-j). The binomial sum equals the kth moment of Z+e(rho)-o(rho) since the moments of Poisson(1) are the Bell numbers. The argument includes the empty restriction and k=0 (zeroth power 1). For positive even k every such moment is strictly positive by nondegeneracy; for k=0 the multiplier is B_n. The even cardinality of the profile gives equality of complementary weights, hence positivity in every character for odd n. Unnormalized Walsh diagonalization proves strict positive definiteness and invertibility. At n=2 the two profiles are empty and full; the two weight-one characters have multiplier zero, giving rank and nullity two. Direct n=3 enumeration gives weights 5,1,1,5. The all-order argument, not the checker, establishes the sign claim.
residual_risks: No replay of the full recorded finite suite was needed for the exact proof. No assertion about general unprotected odd weights at even n follows.

value.rationale: Positive entries of the counting kernel do not decide signed Fourier coefficients. The result establishes a non-obvious protected sector and the full positive-definite/invertible regime at all odd sizes, despite singularity already at even size two. The shifted-moment formula also gives an exact way to determine the signed marked incidence count without listing partitions of all labels. The value is the structural sign theorem, not the small examples or the classical Bell formula alone.
residual_risks: Does not classify the even-order odd sector or quantify the eigenvalue minimum/conditioning.
